package_info.why_malicious: The package was compromised via its dependencies, which were under the control of a previous maintainer whose npm account was accessed by an attacker. Malicious code was injected into these dependencies, causing the installer to crash intentionally (sabotage). This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and disrupts the installation process for all users.

execution_context.file_location: dependency package(s) of purescript (node_modules of purescript installer)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// Example (reconstructed based on typical sabotage code):
throw new Error('Sabotaged by attacker');
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation (postinstall), the code throws an error, causing the installer to crash and preventing successful installation of the PureScript package.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intentionally crashing the installer is a clear sign of sabotage and serves no legitimate purpose. This disrupts the normal installation process for all users.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package dependencies should not contain code that intentionally throws errors or sabotages the installation process. Expected behavior is to facilitate installation, not prevent it.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Throwing errors may be legitimate if a critical precondition is not met (e.g., missing required environment variable), but not as a blanket sabotage.
key_indicators: Error message indicating sabotage or referencing the attacker
Code present in dependency packages not directly maintained by the main project

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to the npm account controlling dependencies of the purescript installer.
Malicious code is injected into one or more dependencies of the purescript npm installer.
When users attempt to install purescript via npm, the postinstall script in the compromised dependency executes and crashes the installer.
attack_chain.leads_to: Denial of service for users attempting to install purescript

behavioral_signatures: Unconditional error thrown during postinstall phase
Installer or dependency code that intentionally halts installation
Unexpected error messages referencing sabotage or attackers
file_indicators: Modified dependency files in node_modules with sabotage code
Error messages in npm logs indicating sabotage
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for unexpected errors during the postinstall phase, especially errors that are not related to missing dependencies or environment issues. Review dependency code for unconditional error-throwing statements or sabotage messages. Audit package-lock.json and node_modules for dependencies recently updated or controlled by external maintainers. Set a minimum version constraint (>=0.13.2) for purescript to avoid compromised versions.
